Modern.brandNameRationale: Telos is the Greek word for purpose or end-cause, used in naturopathic vitalism to describe the body's inherent direction toward health (the vis medicatrix naturae). Strongest of Agent A's modern row: Phyto Practice is narrow (plants only), Galen & Co. risks reading as a herbal supplement brand. Telos Health is a clean two-word mark with a real philosophical anchor in the tradition.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern naturopathy in 2025+ sits between functional-medicine clinics (Parsley, Forward) and old-school herbalists. Patients are 30-50, often post-conventional-medicine, and want clinical seriousness without the white-coat sell. The opening is a practice that owns the vitalist philosophy without the woo vocabulary.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Parsley Health (parsleyhealth.com) is the functional-medicine peer. Forward (goforward.com) holds the membership-clinic model. Bastyr Center (bastyrcenter.org) is the academic naturopathic peer. We sit smaller, philosophy-led, and clinically credentialled.
Modern.positioningStatement: A naturopathic practice grounded in vitalist philosophy and credentialled clinicians.

targetAudience.primary: 32 to 52. Has been through the standard-of-care for a chronic complaint and wants a longer appointment with a real ND. Reads the practitioner's training before booking. Pays out of pocket without complaint.

dos: Cite vis medicatrix naturae as the framework
donts: Sell supplements at the front desk

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — TELOS HEALTH set in a precise modern serif, with a single small arrowhead form above the O suggesting direction toward an end. The arrowhead alone works as the favicon and on the appointment card.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and patient letters
typography.secondary: Söhne for the booking flow and body
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the philosophical-clinical weight; Söhne keeps the booking flow modern.

Luxury.tagline: A private naturopathic practice in the Kneipp tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Bad Wörishofen, Bavaria is the town where Sebastian Kneipp (1821-1897) established the hydrotherapy practice that became one of the roots of European naturopathy. Strongest of Agent A's place row for luxury: Kos Practice is too quiet for the luxury patient, Butler Hall is academically correct but unromantic. Wörishofen House inherits 150 years of European spa-medicine meaning and sidesteps the Kneipp cosmetics TM — Agent A flagged the surname; the town name is safe.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury naturopathy serves the patient who treats their ND like a private physician — long appointments, no waiting room, the same clinician for every visit. The opening is a practice that revives the European Kurhaus-physician posture without the spa-resort trappings.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Lanserhof (lanserhof.com) holds the European medical-spa tier. Buchinger Wilhelmi (buchinger-wilhelmi.com) is the fasting-clinic peer. Pritikin (pritikin.com) sits adjacent in the US. We sit as the urban consulting practice, not the residential clinic.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A discreet private naturopathic practice in the Kurhaus consulting tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 70. Splits the year between a city and a clinic in the mountains. Has a private GP and a private dentist and wants a naturopath in the same register. Pays the invoice the same day.
behaviors: Travels with the clinician's written protocol

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small embossed door-plate mark — a brass leaf form — sits beneath the wordmark, used on the practice card, the protocol letter, and the surgery door.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and printed material
typography.rationale: A high-contrast classical serif carries the Kurhaus register; the grotesk handles the one digital surface.

Minimal.tagline: A naturopathic practice. Plants. Clinicians. Time.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: Phyto, from Greek phyton — plant. The single Greek root that names what most naturopathic medicine actually does: prescribe and prepare plant-derived remedies. Strongest minimal mark of Agent A's modern row: Telos is philosophical (better for the modern brief), Galen risks reading as a supplement line. Phyto stands alone, one word, one syllable in effect, and tells the patient the entire register.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal naturopathy is a long appointment, a clear note, a small dispensary. The opening is a practice that publishes its prices, its dispensary, and the clinician's licensure — and stops there.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Parsley Health (parsleyhealth.com) is the closest tech-led peer. Forward (goforward.com) holds the membership-clinic model. Local independent NDs compete on relationship. We publish less than any of them.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A naturopathic practice. Published prices. Long appointments. One clinician.

targetAudience.primary: Adults 30-55 who want one ND, sixty minutes, and a clear plant-medicine plan. They've left the functional-medicine clinic over the supplement upsell. They want the appointment to start when it was booked.
behaviors: Books a long initial and a six-month follow-up
Reads the price list before booking

dos: Publish the price list on the home page

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. PHYTO set in a single-weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps. No icon. The wordmark works on the door, the dispensary jar, and the appointment card. That is the whole system.

typography.rationale: One face. The sign, the card, and the dispensary jar all carry the same wordmark.

Corporate.tagline: A multi-site naturopathic partnership in the Lust tradition.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: Benedict Lust (1872-1945) founded the first US naturopathic school in 1901 (Butler, NJ) and effectively named the American naturopathic profession. Strongest of Agent A's heritage row for corporate: the dual Lust & Kneipp risks the Kneipp cosmetics TM that Agent A flagged, the Kneipp Method Practice carries the same risk. Lust alone is safe, historically primary, and lands as a serious clinician-led group rather than a chain.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate naturopathy in 2025+ is consolidating around membership-clinic and integrative-medicine groups. The next tier competes on clinician retention and outcomes data rather than franchise mechanics. The opening is a partnership-model group positioned on clinical seniority and tradition.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Parsley Health (parsleyhealth.com) is the largest functional-medicine peer. Cleveland Clinic Integrative (my.clevelandclinic.org/departments/integrative) holds the academic tier. The Institute for Functional Medicine (ifm.org) trains the practitioners. We sit clinician-led, naturopathy-rooted.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A clinician-led naturopathic partnership grounded in the Lust tradition.

targetAudience.primary: Procurement at self-insured employers, HR directors at large firms, and NDs considering joining a group. They sign multi-year contracts and care about clinician retention, outcomes, and licensure compliance across states.
behaviors: Tracks ND-licensure compliance state by state
Values clinician retention rate as a buying signal

dos: Lead with clinician retention and outcomes
Speak the language of self-insured procurement
donts: Promote individual clinicians on national channels

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark — three stacked leaves abstracted as horizontal strokes — to the left. Reads cleanly on uniforms, signage, and procurement decks.

typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed clinical letters
typography.rationale: Inter scales cleanly across procurement decks; the serif handles the printed clinical letters.

Creative.tagline: A naturopathic practice run like an apothecary.
Creative.brandNameRationale: The tincture — an alcohol extract of a plant — is the core artefact of herbal medicine and the daily craft of a naturopathic dispensary. Strongest of Agent A's craft row for creative: Materia Medica is the textbook and reads academic, Constitutional & Co. is too inside-baseball for a public-facing creative brand. The Tincture Room reads as a designed apothecary — the practice and the dispensary as a single craft object.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative naturopathy sits in the register of a good independent apothecary or perfumer. Patients are design-literate, often in adjacent fields, and want a practice that feels crafted — labels, jars, a printed protocol. The opening is a brand with print-shop, illustrated, apothecary aesthetics.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Anima Mundi (animamundiherbals.com) holds the design-led herbal peer. The Herbalist (theherbalist.com) is the apothecary template. Wooden Spoon Herbs (woodenspoonherbs.com) sits adjacent. We sit as the practice with a dispensary attached, not the brand with a clinic on the side.
Creative.positioningStatement: A naturopathic practice with an apothecary attached.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 48. Editors, designers, chefs. Has a relationship with a perfumer and a stationery shop. Will pay for a tincture that has been considered down to the label.
behaviors: Asks where the bitters were sourced
Buys the dispensary jar for the kitchen
Photographs the labels — once — and never again

dos: Name each dispensary cabinet after a materia medica section
Commission a yearly illustrated plant chart

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a chunky display serif with letterpress impression. The O of ROOM is set as a small woodblock-style apothecary bottle. A standalone bottle mark for labels and the bag tag.

typography.primary: GT Sectra Display for the wordmark and illustrated charts
typography.secondary: GT Sectra Book for the printed protocols
typography.rationale: One family, two cuts. The display reads woodblock; the book weight handles the printed protocols.
